messages:
maria: heads-up: kernel-selector v3 (rolled last night) bumped host CPU and 99p for several mobile-heavy hostpools. flame shows most of the uplift in grpc header decode + pretokenize scan + a spike in small writev syscalls.

maria: flame excerpt:```
26.0%  grpc::http2_reader::read_frames
21.5%  grpc::decode_headers
15.0%  pretokenize_scan
8.4%   kvcache.lookup
6.3%   writev (many <256B iovs)
```

chris: any change in minibatch heuristics with v3? smaller batches or different prefetch/seqlen hints can multiply host-side work.

dave: yes - v3 added a "kv_layout_fingerprint" check and switched kernels when fingerprint mismatched; that change indirectly prefers a kernel variant tuned for short sequences which reduces model cost but increases host parse/fragment churn in mobile flows.

maria: kv miss percent on affected hosts: pre-roll 3.2% -> post-roll 8.9%. raw: lookups 1,800,000 miss 160,200.

maria: ```
kv.lookup.total: 1800000
kv.lookup.miss: 160200  # 8.9% post-roll
kv.lookup.miss.prev: 57600  # 3.2% pre-roll
writev.rate.per_worker: 390/s (was 110/s)
```

rachel: observed more small DATA frames on the wire; tokenization seems to emit partial buffers and the frame assembler flushes early. this lines up with writev increase.

chris: actionable mitigations (short term): 1) ingress-side dynamic coalescer that inspects incoming fragment sizes and coalesces header+first N payload chunks up to 4KB or 10ms, 2) runtime writev aggregator that merges adjacent iovecs under 512B before syscall, 3) kernel-selector fallback gate that considers per-host kv_miss and writev_rate before switching.

dave: longer-term idea: make kernel-selector include a "kv_key_layout_compatibility" score so it prefers kernel variants that keep kv key stride/prefixing stable for live traffic. avoids churny key-layout flips.

maria: can we get a quick microbench? perf-ci-bot: add a header/fragment microbench with 64/128/256/512B fragment permutations across kernels and measure parse cpu + writev_count + kv-miss.

perf-ci-bot: request acknowledged. I'll queue a microbench job and add baseline comparison.

rachel: I'm prototyping the ingress coalescer (node sidecar) - simple buffer with two controls: max_bytes=4096, max_delay_ms=8. will feature-flag it. plan to run a 1% canary on mobile traffic.

chris: i'll own the writev aggregator change in runtime (small PR): group consecutive low-size iovecs into a single iovec with an internal buffer to reduce syscalls. low-risk, can be toggled per-process.

dave: I'll add a metric to kernel-selector: last_switch_kv_miss_delta and last_switch_writev_rate so the selector can consider stability metrics before flip. also adding an emergency auto-revert when combined delta exceeds thresholds (kv_miss + writev growth > X).

maria: owners: rachel -> coalescer PR, chris -> writev-agg PR, dave -> selector gating PR. can we land gated feature flags and run a 2h canary?

rachel: starting canary on hostgroup=mobile-ingress-canary with ff=true for coalescer. initial 10m: cpu -4%, writev -58%, kv_miss unchanged (still monitoring).

maria: good signal. chris any rough ETA for writev-agg?

chris: small change, draft PR in ~2h, can be rolled to canary same day. will include microbench results in PR.

dave: selector gating PR will take a bit more due to metric plumbing, ETA 6h. but we can also temporarily bias selector to prefer the previous kernel for mobile hostpools via config override.

maria: please also add an alert: parse_token_pct = cpu.percent(grpc_decode_headers + pretokenize_scan + http2_read_frames). Pager if parse_token_pct increases >5% over 10m and writev_rate > 250/s.

sre-bot: created incident INC-2026-045 (host-parse-token-uplift) and attached runbook template: check canaries, validate rollback flag, escalate if >30m unresolved.

maria: final notes: Ben in infra ran quick A/B with kernel v2 vs v3 on 20 hosts: v2 p99 -32ms vs v3, cpu -7%, writev -62%. decision: proceed with coalescer and writev-agg immediate canary, selector gating + config-bias on standby if regressions persist.

chris: sounds good. I'll include unit test that asserts per-request writev_count <= 6 for standard mobile request fixtures to catch regressions in CI.

rachel: landing coalescer behind ff and will post telemetry at 30m/2h.

maria: thanks all. creating tracking issue INF-2470 and assigning owners as discussed. will update incident with links to perf-ci microbench and canary dashboards.
